summary: The task loop held up well through repeated compactions. All four tasks were implemented, committed and reviewed one at a time, a final whole-branch review ran, and npm test passes (77/77). The finishing-a-development-branch skill loaded, but Claude Code then stopped with "Autocompact is thrashing". The finishing options (merge, push, keep, discard) were never shown, so it is unclear whether the session "ended in the finishing step".
reasoning: Criteria 1–3 are clearly met, based on git, the npm test output and the Agent dispatch order in the session log. For criterion 4, the agent did enter the finishing skill, but Claude Code stopped it with an autocompact-thrashing error before it presented or carried out any finishing choice. Whether that counts as "ending in the finishing step" is unclear, and the thrashing itself looks like a real problem with how often the controller re-reads files after each compaction. So my verdict is investigate rather than pass.

observations.description: The run ended on Claude Code's 'Autocompact is thrashing' halt during the finishing step, so the user never got the finishing choices. Over about 13 minutes (18:40–18:53) the log shows more than 12 compact_boundary events. After each compaction the controller re-read several skill files (SKILL.md, task-loop.md, task-reviewer-prompt.md, review-and-complete.md, finishing SKILL.md, communication SKILL.md) and the 27.6KB plan.md, which seems to refill the small context window almost straight away. Within its last few turns the controller read finishing-a-development-branch/SKILL.md and communication/SKILL.md twice each. The re-read behavior may be too heavy for a small compaction window.

Startup showed a 'Newer Opus model available — Currently pinned: Opus 5' dialog, even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose 'No'. The banner then showed 'Opus 5.5 · Google Vertex AI'.

The pre-flight scan stopped to ask a long multiple-choice question about test gaps in the plan (unused PASSAGE constants; tests fixed at 8 per file). I answered 'Proceed as you recommend.', and the implementers added extra tests, so the suite has 77 tests instead of the plan's 32.
The final Codex gate was recorded as 'degraded' because Codex is not installed. This is worth flagging if reviewers expect that gate to run.
Startup needed four manual dialogs (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before the prompt appeared, even though the HOWTO says dialog-bypass state is seeded.

criteria.criterion: All four functions exported from src/textstats.js, each with a test file, committed, npm test passes
criteria.evidence: src/textstats.js:141 `module.exports = { wordCount, sentenceCount, topWords, readingTimeMinutes };`. test/ contains wordCount.test.js, sentenceCount.test.js, topWords.test.js and readingTimeMinutes.test.js. git log shows 63b5280 feat: add wordCount, 59afbbc feat: add sentenceCount, d8d9b54 feat: add topWords, f69f271 feat: add readingTimeMinutes, plus 2 test commits. git status is clean. npm test: `ℹ tests 77 ... ℹ pass 77 ℹ fail 0`.

criteria.criterion: Each task reviewed before the next task starts
criteria.evidence: Agent dispatch order from jq over the session JSONL: Implement Task 1 → Review Task 1 → Implement Task 2 → Review Task 2 → Implement Task 3 → Review Task 3 → Task 3 fix round 1 → Re-review Task 3 fix round 1 → Implement Task 4 → Review Task 4.

criteria.criterion: Final whole-branch review after the last task
criteria.evidence: After 'Review Task 4', the log shows Agent 'Final whole-branch review', then 'Fix final review findings', then 'Re-review final fix wave'. The assistant then wrote: 'The re-review came back clean.'

criteria.criterion: Session ends in the finishing step
criteria.evidence: Skill hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch was invoked, and the assistant said 'I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work.' The next message was Claude Code's 'Autocompact is thrashing: the context refilled to the limit within 3 turns of the previous compact, 3 times in a row...' The prompt then sat idle ('Churned for 33m 39s · done 10:53 AM'). No AskUserQuestion or finishing options were ever shown, so I never needed to answer 'Keep the branch as-is'.
